name: Hosea
role: Prophet whose marriage mirrored Israel's unfaithfulness
whenBasis: In the reigns Hosea 1:1 names: Uzziah to Hezekiah in Judah, and Jeroboam II in Israel, in Thiele's reckoning.
summary: Son of Beeri, a prophet to the northern kingdom in its last decades. The LORD told him to marry an adulterous wife, and he married Gomer; their children were named Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah (no compassion) and Lo-ammi (not my people), as signs of judgment. Told to love her again, he bought her back. His book pleads with Israel as a husband and a father pleads, and promises the names will be reversed.
body: “When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called My son,” the LORD says through him; “How could I give you up, O Ephraim?” He speaks against kings made without the LORD, calf-worship at Samaria, and alliances with Egypt and Assyria.
Paul quotes his reversal of the names, “I will call them ‘My people’ who are not My people,” and Matthew his words about the son called out of Egypt.

moments.text: “Out of Egypt I called My son”
